name: Lisa Schmierer
headline: PhD Student (AI x Social Good), TUM | CDTM | LMU | relAI
summary: Computer scientist and journalist interested in the mathematical and computational foundations at the intersection of ML and social justice. Striving to meet global challenges with innovative ideas and technology.

positions.title: Doctoral Researcher
positions.company: relAI Konrad Zuse School of Excellence
positions.description: PhD student at the Social Data Science and AI Lab at the Department of Statistics under the supervision of Prof. Frauke Kreuter and funded by the Konrad Zuse School of Excellence in Reliable AI (relAI). In my work I focus on projects that combine interesting theory with real world impact at the intersection of social justice and theoretical computer science.

positions.title: Data Science
positions.description: Building on GraphRAG, I built an MVP that allows Maltego users to interact with their open source investigations, e.g. by asking questions or finding hidden connections.

positions.title: Data & Software Engineer
positions.description: Building on existing frameworks for microclimate simulation, it is my task to improve microclimate prediction using different ML approaches. I regularly use Docker and GCP for this and also support implementing features in the front- and backend.

positions.title: Internship Science Editor
positions.description: As an intern, I wrote articles for the "Tagesschau", and was the author of TV reports for the science magazine "Nano" and "SWR Aktuell". Furthermore, I worked in various forms for different radio programs like "SWR3" and "SWR1", including live talks and self-spoken reports. In addition, I interviewed numerous people, wrote treatments for TikTok-Videos, and hosted them myself.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: As working student in Java development, I gained experience in large software projects, implemented features in the backend, worked with Docker, Jenkins and AWS among others.

positions.title: Head of Sports Department
positions.company: M94.5 - Ein Angebot der MEDIASCHOOL BAYERN
positions.description:
As the sports department head, I was responsible for all forms of content, including our podcast "Die Sportgondel". I supervised editors and accompanied cooperations with Munich sports clubs. 
Meanwhile, I gained valuable experience in team and employee management. Furthermore, I interviewed and was responsible for hiring new members.

positions.title: iOS App Developer
positions.description:
In a team of eight students, we developed an app that will help people suffering from dry eye disease manage their treatments and keep track of their symptoms. Furthermore, the app enables sharing reports with doctors and includes a section where people can learn about the causes and potential treatments of the disease. 
We practiced Scrum throughout the process.

positions.title: Editorial Intern in Local News Coverage
positions.description: During the internship, I wrote reportages and reports about topics in and around Potsdam. Furthermore, I  maintained live tickers and coverage for various demonstrations as well as the state elections in Brandenburg.

positions.title: Editor
positions.company: M94.5 - Ein Angebot der MEDIASCHOOL BAYERN
positions.description:
From the very beginning, I have been producing reports of daily local happenings as well as sports events, including live coverage of elections. Furthermore, I gained experience as a news editor and spokesperson. 
I regularly worked with audio processing tools and hosted live shows in the regular radio program.

company.name: relAI Konrad Zuse School of Excellence
company.tagline: relAI Konrad Zuse School of Excellence
company.description: relAI’s research mission is to train future generations of AI experts in Germany who combine technical brilliance with awareness of the importance of the reliability of AI. As a central component of the Munich AI ecosystem, relAI is committed to making artificial intelligence more safe, secure, responsible and protective regarding the privacy of individuals. It encourages responsible use to exploit AI’s vast potential for the benefit of humanity, to advance insight into and debate on machine learning including its ethical and societal dimensions, and to strengthen “AI made in Germany”.
